procedure_text: NMST (61.2g, 0.278mol), sodium hypochlorite (500ml, 0.745mol) and ruthenium oxide (1.5g, 0.011mol) were charged into a 1L round bottomed flask. This mixture was heated to reflux temperature under stirring for 6-8hours, cooled to 25-30°C and filtered. The filtrate obtained was further cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH <3 using concentrated hydrochloric acid(120mL, 1.23mol) to form precipitated product (NMSBA).The product obtained was filtered and dried at 50°C under reduced pressure to obtain NMSBA as light yellow solid. HPLC purity > 95%; Yield: 70%; and Melting point: 210-214°C.
procedure_summary: NMST is oxidised at its methyl group to NMSBA with sodium hypochlorite over a ruthenium oxide catalyst, the mixture being held at reflux and then cooled and filtered to remove the catalyst. The filtrate is cooled further and acidified with concentrated hydrochloric acid to precipitate the product, which is filtered and dried under reduced pressure.

ARITHMETIC. The test used here is the MASS-PRECISION INTERVAL, now the convention across this run: propagate the significant figures of the printed MASS to a mole interval, and raise molar_mass_inconsistent only where the printed mole figure falls outside it. That gives both printed numbers the precision they are actually printed with, instead of treating the mass as exact and testing only whether the mole figure rounds. Two of the three printed mass/mole pairs in this section pass and one fails. RUTHENIUM OXIDE PASSES: 1.5 g stands for 1.45 to 1.55 g, which against 133.068 g/mol for RuO2 implies 0.01090 to 0.01165 mol, an interval that contains the printed 0.011 mol. NMST FAILS: 61.2 g stands for 61.15 to 61.25 g, which against 215.230 g/mol for C8H9NO4S implies 0.28411 to 0.28458 mol, and the printed 0.278 mol lies outside that interval, so the pair cannot be reconciled at the precision the patent prints. Read the other way round, 61.2 g / 0.278 mol implies a molecular weight of 220.14 g/mol against the true 215.230, the printed mole figure being about 2.2% low. molar_mass_inconsistent is raised. THIS DEFECT IS NOT LOCAL TO EXAMPLE 1. All three Examples that charge NMST print a mole figure that is low against recomputation, and the same mass-precision test separates them: Example 1, 61.2 g / 0.278 mol, interval 0.28411 to 0.28458 mol, EXCLUDES the printed figure, implied weight 220.14, 2.2% low, fails; Example 2, 5.0 g / 0.023 mol, interval 0.02300 to 0.02346 mol, CONTAINS the printed figure, implied weight 217.39, 1.0% low, passes; Example 3, 20g / 0.088 mol at line 285, interval 0.09060 to 0.09525 mol, EXCLUDES the printed figure, implied weight 227.27, 5.3% low, fails. Example 2 is a control only in the narrow sense that it is the one pair of the three whose deviation is small enough to fall inside the interval its own two-significant-figure mass allows; it is NOT evidence that Examples 1 and 3 are unaffected, and Example 3, which is the worst of the three, has raised the same flag on its own record. The three implied molecular weights, 220.14, 217.39 and 227.27, are not one consistent wrong value, so this reads as mole figures computed or rounded imprecisely example by example rather than as a single wrong molecular weight propagated through the set, and no single correction would fix all three. Every interval bound, implied weight and true mole value in this paragraph is a RECOMPUTATION from the printed masses against RDKit molecular weights; none of them is printed in the patent and none has entered any field of this record. Nothing was corrected. mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised: the patent prints a 70% yield but no product mass, so there is no mass to test against the input moles and no pair that disagrees. The hypochlorite charge is a volume with a mole figure, 0.745 mol in 500 ml or 1.49 M, and the acid 1.23 mol in 120 mL or 10.25 M, neither of which is a mass/mole pair, so neither admits a molecular-weight check.
